entities.name: Great Bridge of Central Yharnam
aliases: the great bridge of central Yanam

facts.text: Early in the game, before encountering any boss, the player hears a distant agonized scream from the rooftops of Central Yharnam, foreshadowing the suffering of the beasts.
The Cleric Beast waits on the Great Bridge of Central Yharnam and has been screaming at the moon for a long time before the player encounters it.
The Sword Hunter Badge item description states that Ludwig was the first of many Healing Church hunters, many of whom were clerics, to transform into hideous beasts.

Clerics of the Healing Church administered and received the old blood as a sacred ritual, believing the resulting transformations were caused by insufficient faith rather than an inherent property of the blood.
Game director Hidetaka Miyazaki stated in an interview that the longer a transformation is suppressed by willpower, the larger and more extreme the resulting beast becomes.
The Cleric Beast has nails driven into its legs, interpreted as the reflexive habit of a healer still trying to apply blood vials to wounds even after losing coherent thought.
The specific identity of the Cleric Beast fought on the Great Bridge is never confirmed in the game.
Lawrence, founder of the Healing Church, became the first cleric beast and is fought separately in the Old Hunters DLC.
Brador, a Healing Church assassin encountered later in the Old Hunters DLC, killed a fellow hunter who transformed into a cleric beast and wears that hunter's scalp as a memento.
Father Gascoigne is the first mandatory boss in Bloodborne, meaning players cannot bypass his fight.
Gascoigne's title 'Father' is a foreign pastoral honorific from outside Yharnam, distinct from the Healing Church's own titles like Vicar.
Gascoigne was partnered as a hunter with a veteran named Henryk, described as gallant.
Gascoigne gave his wife Viola a brooch with a deep red jewel that he found while hunting.
Gascoigne and Viola had two daughters together.
As the hunt wore on Gascoigne, he began to lose memories of his family, including his daughters' voices and Viola's sleeping face.
Viola used a music box, wound by hand and playing a melody meaningful to the couple, to recall Gascoigne back to himself whenever the hunt took him too far.
On the night of the game's events, Gascoigne did not return home, and Viola went looking for him without bringing the music box.
The player finds Gascoigne in the Tomb of Oedon, already transformed and destroying corpses.
Before fully transforming, Gascoigne tells the player 'Beasts all over the shop, you'll be one of them sooner or later' and 'The sweet blood, it sings to me.'
Viola's body is found dead near Gascoigne's transformation site, with her brooch lying beside her; the game leaves ambiguous whether Gascoigne killed her himself or found her body after a mob attack.

The player can use the music box given by Gascoigne's daughter during the boss fight to make Gascoigne pause, clutch his head, and mutter as his humanity briefly resurfaces, creating an opening to attack.
When Gascoigne is defeated, a voice beneath his beast noises seems to say 'Forgive me.'
Returning Viola's brooch to Gascoigne's daughter prompts her to say only the word 'mommy,' after which the window goes silent.
The Healing Church sealed the district of Old Yharnam and burned it entirely, killing both the transformed and the untransformed, officially to contain the scourge of beasts.
The burning of Old Yharnam did not stop the plague, which continued spreading through Yharnam via the Church's ongoing blood ministration in other districts.
Jura, a hunter who helped burn Old Yharnam, later returned to live among its ruins, protecting the remaining beasts from other hunters seeking to kill them.
The Blood-starved Beast is found in a church at the bottom of Old Yharnam and carries an additional toxic/poisonous property alongside standard beasthood from exposure to 'ashen blood.'
The Blood-starved Beast's emaciated appearance reflects an insatiable hunger that is actually a craving for blood rather than food.

The Blood-starved Beast resides specifically in the church where Old Yharnam's residents once received blood ministration from the Healing Church, linking the creature symbolically to the faith that doomed the district.
Defeating the Blood-starved Beast rewards the player with a Tumbling (Thumanrian) Chalice, a ritual artifact of the ancient civilization that first discovered the old blood.
Vicar Amelia prays before the altar of the Grand Cathedral, reciting Healing Church liturgy about communion with the old blood as she transforms into a beast.
The title 'Vicar' is the Healing Church's term for its highest representative, derived from a Latin word meaning a proxy who acts on behalf of another authority.
Amelia received Lawrence's pendant, a symbol of his authority, when she succeeded him as leader of the Healing Church.
Lawrence's skull is kept as a relic on the Grand Cathedral's altar, inscribed inside with the words 'Fear the old blood,' attributed to Willem's warning.
During her boss fight, Vicar Amelia heals herself by pressing her hands together in a prayer-like gesture even after losing coherent thought.
The Witches of Hemwick are actually two beings fought together; defeating one and reducing the other to half health causes a second witch to materialize.

The Witches of Hemwick summon the Madmen of Hemwick, eyeless humanoid servants whose empty eye sockets reflect a philosophy that external sight is a limitation and true perception comes from internal transformation.
Master Willem's doctrine held that true perception requires 'eyes on the inside' rather than reliance on physical eyesight.
The Witches of Hemwick practice rites older than the Healing Church, connected to the Hintertomb chalice dungeon branch beneath Hemwick Charnel Lane.
Hemwick Charnel Lane is the district where Yharnam's dead are processed into materials the Healing Church requires for its operations.

The Shadows of Yharnam are three ancient robed guardians stationed at the forbidden woods before the ascent to Byrgenwerth, each wielding different roles: one with sword and torch, one with a candle staff who summons serpents, and one who heals the group.
The Shadows of Yharnam serve Queen Yharnam, a Thumanrian queen after whom the city was named.
Queen Yharnam appears in a blood vision after Rom's death, shown in ceremonial robes with hands crossed over the child she carried, facing a descending moon.

Queen Yharnam entered a contract with Oedon, a formless great one with no physical body, and bore his child, Mergo; the birth effectively ended her existence, leaving her as a suspended remnant rather than fully dead.
Serpents are symbolically associated with the great one Oedon in Bloodborne's iconography, and the Shadows of Yharnam summon serpents in combat.
The Shadows of Yharnam guard the path toward Byrgenwerth and the lake where Rom hides, protecting the secret tied to Queen Yharnam's tragedy.
Darkbeast Paarl is found in a cell within a section of Yahar'gul's underground jail designated as the Graveyard of the Dark Beast, used by the School of Mensis to imprison captives.
Dark beasts like Paarl are technically undead creatures that generate blue-white electricity along their bones, which may serve as an animating current keeping them from fully dying.
The Spark Hunter Badge reveals that it was crafted in secret by Archibald, an eccentric Healing Church researcher who studied bolt electricity emitted by dark beasts.
Archibald worked using methodology closely following Byrgenwerth's approach and created weapons such as the Tonitrus and Tiny Tonitrus, which were not widely adopted by the Church.
All items created by Archibald are found in or around Yahar'gul, suggesting he worked within School of Mensis territory.
The most coherent reading is that Darkbeast Paarl was Archibald's primary research subject for his experiments replicating dark beast electricity.
A tunnel is clawed through stone from Paarl's cell toward the wall separating Yahar'gul from Old Yharnam, suggesting an escape attempt that failed because the door was locked from the Yahar'gul side.
The player is taken to Yahar'gul after being kidnapped from the streets of Yharnam by the Bell-ringing Women who served the School of Mensis.
The One Reborn is a boss composed of a mass of fused human bodies, animated by a School of Mensis ritual using remains of processed victims.
During the fight against The One Reborn, chime maidens continuously heal and empower the creature while attacking the player.
